subject: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and timeline options - Finovo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@finovo.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and timeline options - Finovo

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier today — really helpful to understand Finovo's latency targets and the reporting/compliance constraints you flagged. As promised, I attached an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a short set of discovery notes to capture what we discussed.

Quick recap of the call highlights:
- Primary use case: in-app assistant for underwriting workflows (low-latency token generation, embeddings for docs)
- Key success metrics: p95 generation latency < 250ms, monthly cost per 100k requests target <$2,000
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 evidence, customer-managed KMS for keys, audit logs retention 13 months
- Decision stakeholders: Jordan (Head of AI), Priya Singh (Procurement), Evan Ross (CTO) — please confirm if this list looks right.

Attached: Finovo-MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones) and Discovery-Notes-20260210.pdf (call notes). Also shared a live copy here: https://redwoodgdrive.company/Finovo/MAP-v1

Proposed MAP (high level) — pick a timeline option that works for you, and I can update the spreadsheet accordingly:
Option A (Conservative) — 10-week track
  • Week 1: Stakeholder alignment & legal intake (Finovo: Jordan, Priya; Redwood: me, legal)
  • Week 2–3: Security questionnaire + SOC 2 evidence transfer (Finovo: Priya; Redwood: security)
  • Week 4–5: POC deployment + performance tuning (Finovo: infra lead; Redwood: Dev Patel)
  • Week 6: Eval & quality checks (Finovo product)
  • Week 7–8: Contract & pricing finalization (Procurement)
  • Week 9–10: Rollout planning & go-live prep

Option B (Accelerated) — 6-week track (assumes fast procurement turnaround and SOC 2 evidence already in hand)
  • Week 1: Stakeholder alignment + legal intake
  • Week 2: Security docs + initial POC environment setup
  • Week 3–4: POC run & performance tuning
  • Week 5: Contract terms & pricing
  • Week 6: Go/no-go and rollout planning

Key dependencies:
- SOC 2 report or security evidence access by Week 2 (Procurement/Security)
- Test dataset and sample traffic from Finovo for realistic perf tuning (Product/Infra)
- Legal point of contact to run SOW/Procurement redlines

Ask: can you confirm the stakeholder list and which timeline option you'd prefer? If Option B is viable, what internal approvals would we need to accelerate? If Option A is safer, we can set a target close date of 2026-04-24.

Next steps I propose after you confirm stakeholders/timeline:
- I'll send an updated MAP (tracker) and schedule a 30-min MAP kickoff meeting with all stakeholders
- Dev will prepare an initial POC runbook and Redwood will share a SOC 2 evidence bundle (security redaction as needed)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and timeline options - Finovo

Marissa — thanks for the fast follow-up and the clear MAP. Appreciate the two timeline options; both are useful. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Stakeholders: that list looks right. I'll add Evan Ross (CTO) to the thread separately, and Priya is our procurement lead (looped). I'll cc our infra lead, Samir Patel, on the kickoff once we lock timing.

2) SOC 2: we do not have anything to share publicly right now; we'll need Redwood to provide the SOC 2 report redacted or the equivalent evidence. Priya — can you confirm what format Finovo needs from vendors (typical procurement minimums)?

3) Timeline: Option B would be ideal — p95 latency is a high priority and we want to move quickly. That said, procurement usually needs 3 weeks for contract/PO review at minimum. If we do Option B for technical onboarding, procurement slip could push final close to late March. Can you put a placeholder target close date of 2026-03-28 in the MAP (we can tighten after procurement feedback)?

4) Dependencies: we can provide a sample of anonymized test traffic and a small subset of documents for embedding tests. I'll coordinate that with Samir.

If you can update the MAP with a placeholder close date of 2026-03-28 and include an explicit row for who provides SOC 2 evidence and how it'll be delivered, that'd be great. Also please confirm Redwood's SE lead for the POC (is that Dev Patel?).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Hale
Head of AI, Finovo
jordan.hale@finovo.com | (212) 555-0199
